clue.text: False move by state leads to tougher economic policy

parts.note: MISS is the abbreviation for the US state of Mississippi

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following three words are taken

explanation.surface: A government's slip is blamed for a harsher austerity programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble or blunder, literally or figuratively, is a wrong step taken.

clue.text: Party-pooper like Scrooge losing pounds

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Dickens's Scrooge is a byword for meanness
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A killjoy behaves like Scrooge after losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a misery (or misery guts) is a gloomy person who spoils the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for a habitually gloomy killjoy.

clue.text: Junior minister abused after reforming party

indicators.note: the word abused is taken after being reshaped into a new order

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a political party

explanation.surface: A junior government minister is abused after a party shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder and 'after reforming' is the indicator. The minister is a church minister, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric ranking below a deacon, so a junior member of the ministry.

clue.text: Capacitor in better order for vicar of Bray?

definitions.meaning: a small adjustable capacitor used for fine tuning a circuit
comparative of trim, meaning neat and well kept
the vicar in the song kept changing his religion to keep his post, a time-server

explanation.definitionFit: The word names an adjustable electrical component, means neater, and describes someone who shifts allegiance opportunistically.

clue.text: Sound heard: brass in Chinese accompaniment

indicators.note: the word for sound is taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: to plumb is to sound or measure a depth
brass and sauce both mean cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A brass instrument is heard accompanying a Chinese melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is a verb, to plumb; 'brass' is cheek, which is SAUCE in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum sauce is a sweet dipping sauce served with Chinese dishes such as crispy duck.

clue.text: Healer with brown paper form given gas

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so the letters of the word given are rearranged

parts.note: AR is the chemical symbol for argon, a noble gas

explanation.surface: A medic arrives with a paper sheet and some anaesthetic gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges GIVEN into VINEG. The definition recalls the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill, where Jack mends his head with vinegar and brown paper.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the sour condiment and paper were the remedy applied to Jack's broken head.

clue.text: Prophetic article taken from church HQ

indicators.note: the article is removed from the word for church headquarters

parts.note: the Vatican is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A prophetic text is removed from the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatic is a literary adjective meaning prophetic or oracular, from Latin vates, a seer.

clue.text: Not a source of wealth? European one proposed

parts.note: no means not, as in no better
a mine yields gold or minerals, a source of riches

explanation.surface: A candidate from Europe admits to not being rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for a post or award.

clue.text: Grand US city raised dead duck

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada

explanation.surface: A grand American city brought up a dead duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' turns the Nevada city round to ONER; a dead duck is a lost cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for someone or something doomed or finished.

clue.text: Ladder constantly left out for absconders

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run, a line of laddered stitches

indicators.note: the letter for left is put out of the word

parts.note: constantly means always

explanation.surface: Escapees keep leaving a ladder behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is British for a run in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaways are those who have fled or escaped, people who abscond.

clue.text: Handle fuel block like this in first place

indicators.note: says the piece for like this goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: so can mean in this way, like this
a briquet (also briquette) is a compressed block of coal dust used as fuel

explanation.surface: Instructions for picking up a fuel block, demonstrated first.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for a name or nickname, and the French-derived word means a nickname.

clue.text: Penned by German novelist, introduction to Offenbach opera

indicators.note: something penned by a person is enclosed within them, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: Thomas Mann was the German author of Death in Venice

indicators.note: the opening letter of the composer's name is taken

explanation.surface: A German writer composes the prologue to an Offenbach opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Offenbach's opera, but the answer is by Massenet (also set by Puccini as Manon Lescaut).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Massenet's opera about the tragic heroine Manon Lescaut.

clue.text: Discharge in auditor's chamber

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word for chamber is taken as heard

parts.note: a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: Some leak has appeared in the accountant's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant, but here means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, an old word for mucus.

clue.text: Head of Sport once breaking promise about rugby players

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Sport is taken
the letters of once are broken up and rearranged
the word for promise is turned round

parts.note: to give one's word is to promise

explanation.surface: A sports chief once went back on an undertaking concerning rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges ONCE into ECON, and 'about' turns WORD into DROW.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the locks are the forwards who pack down behind the front row of the scrum.

clue.text: Spymaster involved in cracking cryptic clues with due caution

indicators.note: the spymaster's letter becomes involved in, that is placed within, the other letters
the words cryptic clues are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief sets about solving cryptic clues carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' rearranges CRYPTICCLUES into CIRCUSPECTLY, and M goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting circumspectly means looking around before acting, wary and prudent.

clue.text: Remarkable bird given time inside

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the bird's name

parts.note: the starling is a common songbird

explanation.surface: A notable bird has been given a period indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising or striking, so something remarkable.

clue.text: Catch up with Spanish runner unless extremely gloomy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
a river runs, and the Ebro is a river in Spain

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word unless are taken

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with a Spanish athlete, unless the mood is too dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN; the 'runner' is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenebrous is a literary word for dark and shadowy, from Latin tenebrae.

clue.text: Engineer may scorn NICAM and the like

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An audio engineer may sneer at the NICAM sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' is a verb rearranging MAY SCORN. NICAM is a digital stereo TV sound standard whose name abbreviates near-instantaneous companded audio multiplex.
explanation.definitionFit: NICAM is an example: a word formed from the initials of a phrase.

clue.text: Payment requiring careful thought

definitions.meaning: in law a payment or reward given in exchange for a promise

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the price given in a contract and the act of thinking carefully.

clue.text: Police officer hugging tree sent up briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up reverses the whole assembly
the officer's letters hug, that is surround, the tree

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
the rowan is the mountain ash tree

explanation.surface: A constable embraces a tree and is quickly ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' makes DROWANI, which 'sent up' turns round in this down clue; the tree is the mountain ash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in short, to sum up concisely.

clue.text: Head of worldwide agency being replaced by one old dramatist

indicators.note: names the letter to be swapped: the first letter of the word worldwide
one letter of the agency is swapped out for new letters

parts.note: UNESCO is the United Nations cultural agency
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The chief of a global agency was replaced by a single veteran playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The U of UNESCO, the first letter of 'worldwide', gives way to IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Ionesco was a Romanian-French playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd, who died in 1994.

clue.text: Accept lift

definitions.meaning: to agree to an offer or challenge
to raise or pick something up

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to accept an offer and to raise something physically.

clue.text: Louts hang out for violent attack

indicators.note: out signals the letters being put out of their order

explanation.surface: Thugs loiter about, looking for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LOUTS HANG.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, overwhelming assault or barrage.

clue.text: Female securing a large African belt

indicators.note: the female pronoun secures, that is encloses, the letter A

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A woman fastens a big African belt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahel is the semi-arid strip of land south of the Sahara across Africa.

clue.text: Cover for head of private and public transport

parts.note: a GI is a US private soldier
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A head cover for a private soldier and for bus travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibus is a collapsible opera hat, named after its French inventor.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom reflected in great roll

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the whole of what follows is reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 standing as I
a bun is a sweet bread roll

explanation.surface: An old realm is mirrored in a big bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: AIBUN read backwards. The held clue's stray 'ne' is text from the next column.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an old African realm on the Nile, south of Egypt.

clue.text: Brute circling crop circles

indicators.note: to circle round is to turn back, so the crop's word is read in reverse

parts.note: hay is a crop grown and cut for fodder
O is a circle, so circles are two Os

explanation.surface: A thug is seen walking round crop circles in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' turns the fodder crop round to YAH; the circles are not crop circles but two round letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the Yahoos are brutish humans, so the name means a coarse lout.

clue.text: In the sea, most unusual to find sulphur

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the word for the sea

parts.note: the briny or brine is a name for the sea

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of most arranged out of the usual order

explanation.surface: Finding sulphur at the bottom of the ocean is a rare event.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is the old biblical name for sulphur, the fire-and-brimstone element.

clue.text: Stroke old coin

definitions.meaning: an oblique stroke or slash used in writing
a gold coin of the late Roman empire

explanation.definitionFit: The slash mark took its name from the Roman gold coin, whose abbreviation it once marked.

clue.text: Paint work somewhere in Derbyshire

parts.note: gloss is a shiny paint
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Painting work being done at a house in Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: GLOSSOP is a market town in Derbyshire, an English county in the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossop is a town in the High Peak area of the English county.
